zh.title: 達美航空9月6日起復飛紐約－特拉維夫航線
zh.summary: 達美航空確認；9月6日復飛；紐約至特拉維夫
body: 達美航空（Delta Air Lines）已確認將於近日恢復飛往以色列的直飛航班。據AeroTime報導，達美航空於2026年8月26日表示，紐約甘迺迪國際機場（JFK）與班古力昂國際機場（TLV）之間的每日航班將於2026年9月6日開航。
第一家從紐約出發的班機預計於9月7日抵達以色列，並於當天返回JFK。該航班將使用達美航空的空中巴士A330-900neo客機執飛。達美航空表示，在審視中東地區安全環境後決定復航，該公司發言人強調，透過與航空主管機構及政府部門協調，將持續密切監控局勢。

en.title: Delta confirms resumption of New York-Tel Aviv flights from September 6
en.summary: Delta confirms; daily New York-Tel Aviv flights to resume September 6
body: Delta Air Lines has confirmed that its first non-stop flights to Israel will restart soon, with the resumption of its New York to Tel Aviv service. On August 26, 2026, Delta said daily flights between New York John F. Kennedy International Airport (JFK) and Ben Gurion International Airport (TLV) will start on September 6, 2026.

The first flight departing New York will arrive in Israel on September 7, 2026, and return to JFK later that day. The flight will operate on the company's Airbus A330-900neo aircraft. Delta stated it would recommence the route following a review of the security environment, adding in a statement that 'The safety and security of our customers and employees remain our top priority,' and that it will continue to coordinate with aviation authorities and government agencies.

zh.title: Britten-Norman測試首架英國產Islander
zh.summary: Britten-Norman測試首架英國產Islander；預計9月試飛
body: 英國飛機製造商Britten-Norman已開始針對將生產線遷回英國後製造的首架Islander客機進行地面測試。該公司於2026年8月26日表示，該架客機在成功接通電源後，已於7月30日在懷特島的賓布里奇（Bembridge）工廠完成出廠亮相。
此架新機在完成預計於2026年9月展開的試飛作業後，將交付給福克蘭群島政府航空服務隊（FIGAS）。在出廠前，工程團隊已完成發動機、螺旋槳、整流罩、電氣系統、煞車系統及飛行控制面的安裝作業。
此外，第二架機身目前正於生產線上推進，後續飛機的零組件亦在製造中。Britten-Norman曾於2023年6月宣布，因羅馬尼亞生產成本上升，決定將自1967年開始生產的Islander機型生產線重新遷回賓布里奇。

en.title: Britten-Norman begins ground testing of first UK-built Islander aircraft
en.summary: Britten-Norman has begun ground testing the first Islander aircraft built in the UK following production reshoring.
body: Britten-Norman has begun ground testing the first Islander aircraft built in the UK since returning full production to Great Britain. On August 26, 2026, the company stated that the aircraft rolled out at its Isle of Wight facility in Bembridge on July 30, 2026, after electrical power was successfully applied.

The aircraft is scheduled to begin flight testing in September 2026, after which it will be delivered to the Falkland Islands Government Air Service (FIGAS). Prior to rollout, technicians installed the aircraft's engines, propellers, cowlings, electrical systems, brakes, and flight control surfaces and mechanisms.

A second airframe is currently progressing through the assembly line while components for follow-on aircraft are under manufacture. Britten-Norman had announced in June 2023 that Islander production would return to Bembridge from Romania due to rising manufacturing costs.

zh.title: 印度天翔簽約諾埃米擬購15架兩棲飛機
zh.summary: 印度天翔與諾埃米簽約 擬購15架兩棲飛機 計劃2030年前交付
body: 印度專門經營水陸兩用飛機的運營商SkyHop與挪威公司NOEMI Aerospace（原名Elfly Group）簽署了諒解備忘錄（MoU），據此SkyHop將有權收購最多十五架NOEMI的兩棲飛機。來源文本明確記載：「SkyHop , has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with Norwegian firm NOEMI Aerospace (formerly Elfly Group) to acquire up to 15 of its amphibious aircraft。」
根據協議內容，SkyHop計劃在2030年前透過購買、租賃或兩者結合的方式，引進多達十架NOEMI飛機。來源引用：「SkyHop plans to introduce up to 10 NOEMI aircraft by 2030 through purchase, lease, or a combination of both。」

作為其在印度建立專屬水陸兩用機網絡的一部分，SkyHop的初期營運將重點放在連接拉克沙群島與印度本土。來源說明：「As part of its plans to build a dedicated seaplane network in India, SkyHop’s initial operations will focus on connecting the islands of Lakshadweep and the mainland。」
公司同時設定目標，到財政年度2030年前擁有多達四十架飛機的艦隊。來源記載：「The company is targeting a fleet of up to 40 aircraft by FY2030。」

NOEMI正在研發其首架飛機為全電動水陸兩用機，可在水面及普通跑道起降，設計載客九人並可加一至兩名機師。來源指出：「NOEMI’s first aircraft is being developed as a fully electric amphibious aircraft that can operate from both water and conventional runways. It is designed to carry nine passengers and one or two pilots。」

隨著此次協議，NOEMI的商務管線已超過九十架航空器，涵蓋歐洲、北美洲與亞洲市場。來源說：「With agreements now spanning operators and markets across Europe, North America and Asia, the agreement with SkyHop brings NOEMI’s commercial pipeline to more than 90 aircraft。」

en.title: India's SkyHop Signs MoU to Acquire Up to 15 NOEMI Amphibious Aircraft
en.summary: SkyHop signs MoU with NOEMI to acquire up to 15 amphibious aircraft by 2030
body: SkyHop, India’s dedicated seaplane operator, has entered into a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with Norwegian firm NOEMI Aerospace, which was formerly known as Elfly Group, to acquire up to fifteen of NOEMI’s amphibious aircraft. The source explicitly states: “SkyHop , has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with Norwegian firm NOEMI Aerospace (formerly Elfly Group) to acquire up to 15 of its amphibious aircraft.”

Under the terms of the MoU, SkyHop plans to introduce a maximum of ten NOEMI aircraft into its fleet by the year 2030. These aircraft may be obtained through outright purchase, lease arrangements, or a combination of both financing methods. The source quotes: “SkyHop plans to introduce up to 10 NOEMI aircraft by 2030 through purchase, lease, or a combination of both.”

As part of its broader strategy to establish a dedicated seaplane network across India, SkyHop has indicated that its initial flight operations will concentrate on linking the Lakshadweep islands with the Indian mainland. The source explains: “As part of its plans to build a dedicated seaplane network in India, SkyHop’s initial operations will focus on connecting the islands of Lakshadweep and the mainland.”
SkyHop has set a target to grow its fleet to no more than forty aircraft by the close of the fiscal year 2030. The source notes: “The company is targeting a fleet of up to 40 aircraft by FY2030。”

NOEMI is currently developing its inaugural aircraft as a fully electric amphibious platform capable of operating from both water surfaces and conventional runways. The design calls for a capacity of nine passengers along with space for one or two pilots. The source details: “NOEMI’s first aircraft is being developed as a fully electric amphibious aircraft that can operate from both water and conventional runways. It is designed to carry nine passengers and one or two pilots.”

The recent agreement between SkyHop and NOEMI has pushed NOEMI’s total commercial pipeline beyond ninety aircraft, encompassing interest from operators in Europe, North America and Asia. The source affirms: “With agreements now spanning operators and markets across Europe, North America and Asia, the agreement with SkyHop brings NOEMI’s commercial pipeline to more than 90 aircraft.”
